documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute COPD Exacerbation with Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening shortness of breath and cough x 4 days, acute worsening tonight.
HPI:
50 yo female with known COPD (GOLD 3 by prior PFTs, FEV1 42% predicted) presents via EMS at 01:25 with progressive dyspnea.
Onset of coryza and productive cough 4 days ago, sputum changed from clear to thick yellow-green.
Used home albuterol MDI q2h with minimal relief; ran out of canister yesterday evening.
Tonight became unable to walk to bathroom without stopping twice.
Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today.
Denies chest pain, hemoptysis, fever, leg swelling, or calf pain.
No sick contacts other than grandchild with URI symptoms last week.
Smoker, 1 ppd x 32 years, approx 32 pack-years, still smoking 5-6 cigs/day.
No home oxygen. Prior COPD admission 14 months ago, no prior intubation. One prior BiPAP use in ED.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
COPD, chronic bronchitis phenotype.
Osteoporosis, T-score -2.6.
GERD.
Anxiety.
Remote left wrist fracture.
HOME MEDICATIONS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily.
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5, 2 puffs BID (reports missing doses often).
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4-6h PRN.
Pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
Sertraline 50 mg PO daily.
Calcium/vitamin D daily.
ALLERGIES:
Sulfa - rash.
SOCIAL / FAMILY:
Lives with wife in a second-floor apartment, 12 steps to entry. Works part time as a cashier. No alcohol, no illicit drugs.
Father had emphysema. No family history of asthma.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vitals 03:05: T 37.4, HR 118, BP 148/86, RR 32, SpO2 89% on 4L NC.
Gen: ill-appearing, diaphoretic, intermittently drowsy.
HEENT: pursed-lip breathing, dry mucous membranes, no JVD assessed as elevated.
Resp: Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Resp: diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, decreased air movement at bases, no focal crackles.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness, warm.
Neuro: arousable to voice, oriented to person and place, follows simple commands, no asterixis appreciated, no focal deficit.
Skin: intact, no rash.
DATA:
WBC 14.2, Hgb 13.8, Plt 288. Na 137, K 4.1, Cl 96, HCO3 31, BUN 14, Cr 0.7, glucose 168.
Lactate 1.6. Resp viral panel sent. Blood cultures x2 drawn 02:05.
CXR portable: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no consolidation, no effusion, no pneumothorax.
ASSESSMENT:
50 yo female with severe COPD presenting with acute exacerbation likely triggered by viral URI, now with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure and hypercapnic encephalopathy.
PLAN:
1. Resp failure: continue BiPAP 14/6, wean as mentation and pH improve. Repeat ABG in 2h. RT at bedside. Titrate to SpO2 88-92%.
2. COPD exacerbation: scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h and q2h PRN. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours.
3. Abx: azithromycin 500 mg IV daily plus ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily for purulent sputum.
4. Monitor glucose q6h given steroids.
5. Hold sertraline while somnolent; resume when awake and taking PO.
6. Smoking cessation counseling, nicotine patch 14 mg offered.
7. Telemetry, step-down unit admission. Discussed escalation plan with pt and wife.
8. DVT ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 - Step-Down Unit
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt awake and conversant this morning, now speaking in full sentences. Remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
Off BiPAP at 12:30 yesterday to 4L NC, tolerated daytime. Reports cough looser, sputum lighter yellow.
Slept about 5 hours with mask on overnight, complains of mask pressure over bridge of nose.
No chest pain. No longer falling asleep mid-sentence per RN and per wife at bedside.
OBJECTIVE:
T 37.1, HR 96, BP 132/78, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 3L NC. Weight 71.4 kg.
Gen: comfortable, sitting up eating breakfast.
Resp: scattered expiratory wheeze upper fields, improved air movement, no accessory muscle use this exam.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no asterixis.
Ext: no edema.
LABS:
ABG 06:20: pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 66 on 3L.
WBC 11.8 (down from 14.2), K 3.6, HCO3 29, Cr 0.7.
Glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale; two coverage doses given overnight (6 units, 4 units).
Resp viral panel: rhinovirus positive. Blood cultures negative at 24h.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation with hypercapnic respiratory failure - improving. Continue nocturnal BiPAP 14/6. Daytime 2-3L NC, target SpO2 88-92%.
2. Continue methylprednisolone 40 mg IV q8h today; plan transition to prednisone 40 mg PO tomorrow if trajectory holds.
3. Continue scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h, taper toward q6h.
4. Steroid hyperglycemia: continue insulin sliding scale q6h with accuchecks, add corrective moderate scale. Diabetes education if persists.
5. Abx day 2 of 5, narrow to azithromycin PO when tolerating.
6. Replace K with 40 mEq PO.
7. PT eval for ambulation with pulse ox.
8. Resume sertraline 50 mg PO daily now that mentation clear.
9. Nicotine patch 14 mg started, cessation counseling reinforced.
10. Continue enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3 - Transferred to Medical Floor
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt off BiPAP since 07:00, no reinstitution needed overnight after 4 hours of use. Slept well.
Ambulated 150 feet in hallway with PT at 10:15, SpO2 nadir 89% on 2L, recovered to 93% at rest within 1 minute.
Dyspnea now only with exertion, MRC 2-3. Cough infrequent, sputum clear.
Appetite good. No nausea. Asking about going home.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.9, HR 88, BP 128/74, RR 18, SpO2 93% on 2L NC, 90% on room air seated.
Gen: alert, pleasant, in chair.
Resp: rare end-expiratory wheeze at right upper field, otherwise clear, good air entry, no accessory muscle use.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Neuro: alert and oriented, nonfocal.
LABS:
Glucose readings last 24h: 256, 198, 214, 176. Total insulin coverage 12 units.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation - much improved, off noninvasive ventilation >24h anticipated. Transfer to medical floor accepted.
2. Transitioned from IV steroid to prednisone 40 mg PO daily at 09:00; plan 5 more days total then stop.
3. Nebs spaced to q6h plus PRN; restart tiotropium and budesonide-formoterol today with inhaler technique teaching by RT.
4. Hyperglycemia: continue sliding scale while on prednisone; trending down. Fasting glucose in AM.
5. Abx day 3 of 5, azithromycin 500 mg PO daily.
6. Continue nocturnal BiPAP available PRN only; RT to reassess.
7. Wean O2 as tolerated; ambulatory sat walk in AM to decide on home O2 need.
8. Continue nicotine patch, cessation plan and pulmonary follow-up.
9. Anticipate discharge HD4 if room air sats acceptable.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation with Acute Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
lines: ADMIT/DISCHARGE: Admitted HD1 via ED, discharged HD4 to home with wife.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute exacerbation of severe COPD with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.
2. Rhinovirus upper respiratory infection.
3. Steroid-induced hyperglycemia.
4. Tobacco use disorder, 32 pack-years.
HOSPITAL COURSE:
50 yo female with severe COPD presented at 01:25 with 4 days of cough and acute dyspnea. SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.

Exam notable for visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time. Somnolent on arrival, arousable to voice but falls asleep mid-sentence; wife reports this is new today.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L, consistent with hypercapnic encephalopathy.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.

Treated with IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours, scheduled albuterol-ipratropium nebs, azithromycin and ceftriaxone. Cultures negative; viral panel positive for rhinovirus. CXR without consolidation.
Glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale; improved as steroids were converted to oral prednisone on HD3.
Mentation cleared by HD2 morning. Off noninvasive ventilation entirely from HD3 07:00. Ambulated 150 feet HD3 with SpO2 nadir 89% on 2L.
HD4: room air sats 91-93% at rest and 90% after 300 feet ambulation - no home oxygen required. Discharged in stable condition.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.8, HR 82, BP 124/76, RR 16, SpO2 92% on room air.
DISCHARGE LABS: WBC 7.6, Hgb 13.4, K 4.2, HCO3 27, Cr 0.7, fasting glucose 142.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 3 more days, then stop.
Azithromycin 500 mg PO daily x 2 more days.
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily.
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5, 2 puffs BID with spacer, rinse mouth after use.
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h PRN dyspnea.
Pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
Sertraline 50 mg PO daily.
Nicotine patch 14 mg daily plus lozenge PRN.
Calcium/vitamin D daily.
FOLLOW-UP:
Pulmonary clinic in 7-10 days with repeat spirometry when stable.
Primary care in 5 days for symptom check and glucose review.
Pulmonary rehab referral placed.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Return for increasing breathlessness at rest, inability to speak in sentences, confusion or drowsiness, fever, or worsening purulent sputum.
Inhaler technique reviewed with RT twice, teach-back adequate. Written COPD action plan given to pt and wife.
No driving while drowsy. Continue smoking cessation; quit date set for day after discharge.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating independently on room air.
